solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Frothy stuff evident in famous sermon

indicators.note: the letters are on view inside the words that follow, so the answer sits within them

explanation.surface: A celebrated sermon is said to contain something frothy, perhaps a mocking verdict on a windy preacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A light whipped dessert or hair foam is a frothy substance, made airy with bubbles.

clue.text: Cycling route away from the centre

indicators.note: cycling a word sends a letter round from one end to the other, here the first letter of the word route goes to the back

explanation.surface: A cycle path that takes riders out of town, away from the city centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Something farther from the middle than the rest is outer, the adjective for the outside part.

clue.text: Upcoming great acts around set before time is right for audience

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the first in the answer
the reversed word goes around the next piece, which sits inside it
in a down clue, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: feats are great or heroic acts
jelly sets, or gels

explanation.surface: A theatre note: a rising performance of great deeds is staged around the set just before curtain time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upcoming' reverses the great acts word, as this is a down clue. Stage directions are given from the actor's side, which is why this is the audience's right.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage directions are given from the actor's viewpoint facing the house, so the actor's left side is the right side as the audience sees it.

clue.text: Someone inventive such as Sheeran gets broadcast?

parts.note: Ed Sheeran is the singer, so his first name is an example of a man named Ed
a programme that is being broadcast is on air, i.e. it is on

explanation.surface: Is a singer like Ed Sheeran inventive enough to get on the radio?
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Edison was the prolific American inventor of the phonograph and an electric light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison is the archetypal inventor, so he exemplifies someone with an inventive mind.

clue.text: Public transport retains functions causing concern

indicators.note: keeping something inside, so the next piece sits within the first

parts.note: a bus is a form of public transport
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: The bus service keeps some functions that are giving cause for worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causing' is a link; the definition is 'concern' in the sense of a matter or affair, as in 'none of your business'.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter that is one's affair or responsibility is one's concern, as in 'mind your own'.

clue.text: Cobblers start off agitation with landed gentry ultimately feeling unassailable?

parts.note: cobblers is British slang for nonsense, as is bunk

indicators.note: the first letter is taken off the following word

parts.note: ferment is a state of agitation or unrest
alit is a past tense of alight, to land or come down

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word gentry is used

explanation.surface: Talk of nonsense and unrest among the landed gentry who feel they cannot be touched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cobblers' is British slang for rubbish talk; 'start off' removes F from FERMENT to leave ERMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege mindset in which a group feels defended against all criticism describes the attitude of feeling beyond attack, hence the question mark.

clue.text: One has unlimited potential for development, putting bow on short string instrument

definitions.text: One has unlimited potential for development

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it, so it comes first

parts.note: the stem is the bow, the front of a ship

indicators.note: short means cut, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: the cello is a bowed string instrument

explanation.surface: A cellist puts a bow to a cut-down instrument, a player with unlimited potential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like the cellist's bow but is the front of a ship; 'short' drops the final O from CELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Undifferentiated biological units can develop into many specialised kinds, so such a unit has unlimited potential.

clue.text: Hopeless, having been elected today?

parts.note: now means at present, today
a candidate who has been elected is in office, or in

explanation.surface: A politician feels despairing despite winning the vote today.
explanation.definitionFit: A situation where every outcome is bad is unwinnable, so there is no hope of success.

clue.text: In Washington keep an eye on certain houses to hide Liberal

definitions.text: In Washington keep an eye on

indicators.note: a word that houses others contains them, so the next pieces go inside it

parts.note: sure means certain
to veil something is to hide it

explanation.surface: A spy in the US capital watches certain houses where a Liberal is hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Washington' marks an American usage: the verb is a back-formation chiefly used in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: An American verb meaning to keep under watch, a back-formation from surveillance, so it equals watch or monitor.

clue.text: Expert admitting set song note is discordant

indicators.note: letting others in, so the next pieces go inside the first

parts.note: an ace is an expert
a TV set
an aria is an operatic song

explanation.surface: An expert lets a television song and a note in, and the result jars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' looks like a verb but is a television set; 'admitting' splits the expert word to take in the other three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in conflict or disagreement with something means being out of harmony, hence discordant.

clue.text: With skill one may be an outstanding nuisance

definitions.text: one may be an outstanding nuisance

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: With enough skill, someone may become a remarkable pest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is literal: the growth stands out from the skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A small growth that protrudes from the skin is an annoying bump, literally standing out.

clue.text: Very unpleasant banker has regrets, displacing knight

indicators.note: one piece pushes another out and takes its place in the word

parts.note: the gnomes of Zurich is a nickname for Swiss bankers
N is the chess notation for knight
rues means regrets

explanation.surface: A banker regrets something after ousting a knight, an ugly business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is not a river but a Swiss financier, a gnome; RUES replaces its N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something horrid or ghastly, especially involving death or injury, is grisly, i.e. very unpleasant.

clue.text: Reckon on wrecking weapon in childish battle

indicators.note: wrecking a word breaks it up so its letters can be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone works out the wrecking power of a weapon in a playground fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A British schoolchildren's game in which a horse chestnut on a string is swung to smash an opponent's.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse chestnut threaded on string serves as the weapon in a traditional British children's game of striking.

clue.text: Audible sounds from stable point

indicators.note: audible means the word is heard, so a word sounding the same is entered

parts.note: horses in a stable make neighs

explanation.surface: Noises can be heard from the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: The Naze is a headland in Essex, England; the word also means a promontory.
explanation.definitionFit: A headland or promontory is a point of land jutting into the sea, as at the Essex headland of that name.

clue.text: Be hugging foot of commander worthy of respect

indicators.note: the clue's two letters wrap around the last letter of the following word, so its bottom letter is replaced by itself wrapped

parts.note: an admiral commands a fleet
the clue word supplies B and E, which hold the final L between them

explanation.surface: Clinging to a commander's feet is presented as honourable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Be hugging foot of' puts B and E around L, the foot (last letter) of ADMIRAL in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Deserving esteem and approval means being estimable, which is a synonym of the phrase.

clue.text: Writer, regressing, left inside to dwell in a wood

indicators.note: going backwards, so the whole assembly is read in reverse
the dwelling word sits within the tree

parts.note: elm is a wood

indicators.note: put within, so the next piece goes into the following word

parts.note: to live is to dwell

explanation.surface: A writer in decline leaves to settle in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressing' reverses the whole assembly of left inside dwell inside the tree, giving ELLIVLEM before the turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Herman Melville was the American novelist who wrote Moby-Dick, so he is a writer.

clue.text: One would almost be tempting: for Arabs, the same

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to entice is to be tempting to someone
al is the Arabic definite article

explanation.surface: Someone almost tempting would find Arabs all alike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims ENTICE to ENTIC; Arabic al- means 'the', as in Al-Qaeda.
explanation.definitionFit: Things exactly alike in every respect are indistinguishable, which is what identical means.

clue.text: Create ski runs, saving run to practise winter sport

indicators.note: runs means the letters move about and are rearranged
saving means except, so one letter of the pool is left out

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A resort makes ski runs, while keeping one aside for some other winter activity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' rearranges CREATESKI less R, which 'saving' leaves out.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding over frozen water on bladed boots is a winter sport, and the verb means to do it.

clue.text: Space connected to ears, relating to non-verbal communication

parts.note: an em is a printer's space
otic is the adjective relating to the ears
on means attached or connected to

explanation.surface: A space linked to hearing that concerns communication without words.
explanation.walkthrough: EM is a printer's measure of space; the order in the clue differs from the answer's.
explanation.definitionFit: A smiley or similar keyboard symbol conveys feeling without words, a form of wordless messaging.

clue.text: Ideal venue for one PM

definitions.meaning: paradise, the perfect place of the Bible's first garden
Anthony ... was a British prime minister in the 1950s

explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is an idyllic place, and Anthony Eden was a British prime minister in the 1950s, so the word fits both meanings.

clue.text: Singular marker of infinitive in Latin with conventional usage

indicators.note: the singular and the infinitive marker go inside the Latin word

parts.note: cum is Latin for with
to marks the infinitive in English, as in 'to go'

explanation.surface: A grammar note: a singular infinitive marker in Latin, with its conventional usage.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as grammar, but CUM is the Latin for 'with'.
explanation.definitionFit: An established practice or habit is a tradition, which is accepted and conventional usage.

clue.text: Linguistic figures recalled area away from coastal town

indicators.note: called back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
one letter is taken out of the word that follows

parts.note: a seaport is a coastal town

explanation.surface: Figures of speech were remembered by someone away from a coastal town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes A from SEAPORT to give SEPORT; 'recalled' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Metaphors and similar figurative expressions are figures of speech, the usual sense of the plural term.

clue.text: Task force reversing attitudes at last?

indicators.note: reversing turns letters round, and here only a stretch is turned
at last limits the turning to the final pair of letters

parts.note: poses are attitudes, postures struck

explanation.surface: A task force changes its attitudes at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing ... at last' swaps the final two letters of POSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A group gathered by a sheriff for a specific job is an ad hoc task force.

clue.text: Attorney-General about to interrupt, rudely touching

indicators.note: around, so the first piece goes outside the second

parts.note: to butt in is to interrupt rudely

explanation.surface: The Attorney-General is about to interrupt and grab someone rudely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' looks to modify 'touching' but belongs with 'to interrupt', giving BUTT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying adjacent and sharing a border means being next to or in contact with, i.e. adjoining.

clue.text: Turbulent as any lake

indicators.note: turbulent means agitated, so the letters are churned into a new order

explanation.surface: Waters are as rough as any lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Nyasa, now called Lake Malawi, is a large lake in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Nyasa is a large African lake, now officially known as Lake Malawi.

clue.text: Two sons trapping black bird

indicators.note: catching something inside, so the next piece goes within

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
B is short for black, as on pencils
S is short for son or sons

explanation.surface: Two boys catch a black bird.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes between the two I's of II, before S.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-billed wading waterbird sacred in ancient Egypt, so an example of a bird.

clue.text: Noble craft protecting lives against bow drawn back

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so the next pieces go inside

parts.note: art means craft or skill
one who lives is, i.e. exists
to can mean against, as in a ladder set to the wall

indicators.note: drawn back means reversed, read the other way

parts.note: a bow is shaped like an arc

explanation.surface: An archer's noble craft guards lives with a bow drawn back against foes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow drawn back' looks like archery, but the bow is a curve, reversed. 'against' as TO is the sense in 'set the ladder to the wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the hereditary upper class is a noble, a person of high rank and title.

clue.text: Church to measure variable space for graves

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
to meter something is to measure it
Y is an algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A church measures a variable plot of space for burials.
explanation.definitionFit: A graveyard or burial ground is an area set aside where the dead are laid to rest.

clue.text: Religious expert to ponder expression of joy or pity

parts.note: to mull something over is to ponder it
ah is an exclamation of pleasure or sympathy

explanation.surface: A theologian considers whether to cry out in joy or pity.
explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim scholar learned in Islamic law and theology, so a religious expert or teacher.
